translationRepairs: Only the Wuyan clan put out a thousand in gold on loan, its interest being one in ten.
Only the Wuyan clan put out a thousand in gold on loan, its interest being tenfold.

Focus unit 其息十之 means interest of ten on the principal (tenfold), not one-in-ten; the next unit’s 息十倍 confirms the same sense. The proposed literal repair corrects that numeral error without adding or dropping content.

When Marquis Wen of Wei was on the throne, Li Kui devoted himself to exhausting the productive power of the land, while Bai Gui delighted in observing how the times shifted; therefore when others cast goods aside he took them, when others seized goods he supplied them.

When Marquis Wen of Wei was on the throne, Li Ke devoted himself to exhausting the productive power of the land, while Bai Gui delighted in observing how the times shifted; therefore when others cast goods aside he took them, when others seized goods he supplied them.
The Wuying Palace Han Shu witness at Chinese Text Project reads 李克, not the corrupted local 李史. Preserve this chapter's reading as Li Ke; Li Kui (李悝) remains an alternate form for the same reformer.
Under Marquis Wen of Wei, Li Kui worked every field for its utmost yield, while Bai Gui thrived on contrarian timing—buying what the market dumped and selling into every rush.
Under Marquis Wen of Wei, Li Ke worked every field for its utmost yield, while Bai Gui thrived on contrarian timing—buying what the market dumped and selling into every rush.

The primary Han Shu witness reads 李克 in this sentence. The idiomatic translation therefore uses Li Ke, while the glossary retains Li Kui (李悝) as the alternate form by which the reformer is commonly known.
